$comment: Known-vulnerable content that is vendored on purpose, and the reason it
is not a BLACKHEART defect. Enforced by audit group 20 in
.github/scripts/gap_audit.py: if an entry stops being vendored, or stops
being byte-identical to the upstream pin, the audit fails. That is the
point -- the file must remain a faithful mirror, not a patched copy.
This is the same rule already applied to the 111 dead links in

policy.rationale: The repository ships no build step, no bundler and no third-party runtime, so it declares no dependency manifest of its own. Every manifest in the tree is vendored. A future contributor adding an authored manifest is a posture change and should be a deliberate, visible decision.

why: It is the test corpus of the vendored `dependency-auditor` skill, a tool whose entire job is to find vulnerable dependencies. Its outdated axios, nodemailer, multer, mongoose, lodash and jsonwebtoken pins are the input that makes the skill demonstrable.

It is vendored, not authored. Editing it would break the byte-identical mirror guarantee that validate.py's integrity check enforces, and would make BLACKHEART's own copy of upstream silently diverge.
It is a `sample-web-app` fixture. Nothing installs it, builds it, ships it or executes it. No lockfile is committed and there is no build step that could pull it in.
Patching it would destroy the very thing it exists to be.
known_vulnerable_fixtures.disposition: ACCEPTED -- do not patch. Re-verify with audit group 20 if the upstream pin moves.
